content: Vaccinations play a critical role in maintaining the health of the adult population. For individuals aged 18 to 64 years, annual vaccinations are recommended. However, according to data from the National Health Interview Survey (NHIS), only 5% of adults at risk for pneumococcal infections receive the pneumococcal vaccine, while 40% of individuals at risk for influenza are vaccinated against the flu. In adults over the age of 65, there has been a significant improvement in adherence to recommended vaccination schedules. Detailed guidelines for adult vaccination schedules have been established, taking into account age and underlying medical conditions. These guidelines also include specific recommendations for special populations and outline contraindications associated with adult vaccinations.
